title: Integrating deep learning and clustering techniques to address imbalanced data in traffic accident severity prediction
abstract: Abstract The rarity and randomness of serious traffic accidents result in highly imbalanced datasets, posing challenges for prediction and interpretation. Although emerging deep learning methods effectively address class imbalance, they are often unstable and may generate unrealistic data. To address this issue, this study proposes using the K-Prototype (KP) clustering algorithm to refine synthetic data, with Gini impurity employed to filter high-quality data by Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP). Subsequently, we develop an evaluation framework to assess the effectiveness of the proposed method, including a systematic comparison of the similarity between synthetic data generated by different resampling techniques and real data, as well as their impact on improving accident severity classification performance. The results show that the proposed method not only maintains data diversity but also enhances feature distribution, with the synthesized data from WGAN-GP-KP outperforming all other methods in accident severity prediction models. Furthermore, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) technique is employed to analyze the factors influencing the severity of traffic accidents. This study offers valuable insights for traffic researchers in addressing imbalanced datasets related to accident severity.
